places.name: Hàm Nguyệt Trang
places.size: The Shore House: the old seat of a small water-arts sect of about 60 people (11 named cultivators, the rest divers, net-menders and pearl-washers), now the sect's lakeside house after the inner halls moved away. About 40 buildings in one walled compound of roughly 150 m, plus pearl sheds along 400 m of shore. Young (founded 410) and small, but it lives off a lake pearl trade, so the shore is busy.
places.where: Region 1, northern Lãnh Nguyệt Lâm. Temperate forest at lake level on the shore of Hạo Nguyệt Hồ, the long silver lake that on the map runs north to south as a narrow blue ribbon beside forest; a rocky ridge stands just north-west. The lake is the biggest on the continent. Water-lean sect, vassal of Tùng Đào Cung; Trầm Bích Đàm, its inner pool, is 90 km away.
places.imagined: A calm early evening in autumn. The lake is pale silver, the birches yellow. Three piers reach into the water and the white ring of the Moon Net sits just off them with the first moon in it. Pearl sheds and drying racks line the shore; boats come in.
places.subject: The place: Hàm Nguyệt Trang, the Shore House of a small water-arts sect, a walled compound of dark timber halls on the shore of a very long silver lake. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle. A grove of pale birches and dark spruce fills the land side; the lake fills the lower half of the frame, pale silver and still, running away to a hazy far end, with a rocky ridge on the far shore to the left. The compound: a rectangular timber-palisaded and low stone-walled enclosure about the size of a large village green, holding some forty buildings, dark-stained timber halls with grey tile roofs set around three small courtyards, a gate house on the landward side, a long pearl-washing hall, dormitories, kitchens and boat sheds. At the lake edge rises a slender three-roofed moon-viewing tower, the tallest thing on this stretch of shore, and three long slim wooden piers run out from the compound over the water, each a hundred metres long with small lantern posts. Signature element: just beyond the piers, a perfect ring of white stones breaks the surface of the shallows, some forty metres across, enclosing a circle of water so calm that it holds the whole reflection of the sky; outside the ring the water is lightly rippled. Life at scale: along the shore on both sides of the piers stretch long rows of pearl sheds on stilts, drying racks of nets and baskets, and lines of pearl-farm stakes in the shallows; a dozen small skiffs, divers' rafts, and tiny figures sitting in a line on the end of the pier facing the ring. A narrow footpath wanders into the birches toward a few outbuildings. Light and season: early autumn evening, golden light from the upper left, yellow birch leaves, long soft shadows toward the lower right, a faint first moon already visible and mirrored in the ring.

places.name: Quy Điểu Trấn
places.size: A walled lake-port town of about 1,500 roofs inside a wall roughly 600 m by 450 m, perhaps 6,000 people, with a harbour basin and a long fringe of nest poles. A town (a thousand or more roofs), not a city, but busy: it is the pearl market of the lake shore.
places.where: Region 1, northern Lãnh Nguyệt Lâm. Sea-level temperate forest on a broad bay of the long lake; on the map a wide blue bay with a small bump of shore and forest all around, a Tùng Đào town and port. Nearest: Hàn Yên Thôn 152 km, Ngưng Yên Nhãn spirit vein 180 km, Bách Điểu Lâm forest 195 km.
places.imagined: An autumn morning when the birds return. Every nest pole along the shore and every roof ridge is crowded with arriving flocks, pearl buyers are walking down the quays, and the sky over the bay is full of wings.
places.subject: The place: Quy Điểu Trấn, a walled lake-port town of grey roofs, famous for a shoreline of tall birch poles each crowned with a straw nest basket. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle, a flat shore on the edge of a wide bay of the great silver lake that fills the lower third of the frame; birch and spruce forest stands behind the town to the upper edge, autumn-gold. The town: a rectangular wall of grey stone about 600 metres long, with four gate towers and a taller gate house on the lake side, enclosing roughly fifteen hundred roofs of grey tile in tight blocks around a main street running gate to harbour, a central market square with a grey pearl-market hall, a clan hall, warehouses and shop rows, and small courtyards; smoke rises from chimneys. A curved stone harbour wall encloses a basin with a few dozen moored skiffs, barges and fishing boats, and stone quays with stacked baskets and nets. Signature element: along the whole shoreline beyond the wall, in long straight rows and double rows, stand hundreds of tall thin pale birch poles, each topped by a round straw nest basket, and the poles, the basket rims and the roof ridges are crowded with birds, thousands of tiny dark specks, with more flocks wheeling in the sky over the water and descending in wavering lines. Between the poles and the harbour wall: a pebble beach, drying racks, a thin rim of pale ice along the very edge of the bay. Life at scale: carts and porters on the road from the main gate, pearl buyers in tiny knots on the quay, children dwarfed by the poles. Light and season: a clear cold autumn morning, golden light from the upper left catching the pole tops and the birds' wings, long soft shadows to the lower right.

places.name: Tuyết Lộc Thôn
places.size: A herders' village of about 12 low log houses, a few smokehouses, a corral and a short jetty, perhaps 80 people. All of it fits in a patch some 150 m across; the antler arch is about 8 m tall, the one big thing.
places.where: Region 1, north shore of Hạo Nguyệt Hồ at sea level. On the map a deep open bay of the lake with forest and a grey rocky outcrop on the north-east shore. A Hàm Nguyệt Trang village, in snowy temperate forest. Nearest: Tuyết Báo Cương beast lair 79 km.
places.imagined: Early winter, first snow. Reindeer are grazing the lichen between the houses and the water, a grey plume rises from a smokehouse, and the herders have just added this year's finest antlers to the gate arch.
places.subject: The place: Tuyết Lộc Thôn, a small reindeer herders' village on a snowy lake shore. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle but close, so the whole village fills the middle of the frame; the open lake lies in the lower part, grey-blue with a rim of shore ice, and dark spruce forest with a grey rocky outcrop stands behind the village to the upper right. The village: twelve low log houses with grey tile and turf roofs dusted with snow, set in two loose rows along a trampled snow street running from the shore up to the forest edge, each with a woodpile, a drying rack for fish and hides, and a small yard; four low smokehouses in a line along the shore; a big fenced winter corral of rough poles on the left, holding a herd of some sixty reindeer as tiny tawny specks, with more grazing lichen pockets on the open white ground. A short plank jetty runs into the lake with two small skiffs tied to it. Signature element: at the village's entrance on the street stands a tall rough gate arch built entirely of interlocked shed reindeer antlers, pale bone-coloured, as tall as a three-storey house, doubled in height since the first one, a few extra antlers newly stacked on top, with a small stone cairn at its foot. Life at scale: three or four tiny figures leading reindeer, a sledge on the shore track, a child at the arch, smoke thin and vertical. Light and season: early winter afternoon, warm golden light from the upper left catching the antlers and the snow, soft blue shadows lengthening to the lower right.

places.name: Hàn Yên Thôn
places.size: A fishing village of about 25 grey-roofed houses with tall stone chimneys, a bell post, some boat sheds and a few drying racks, perhaps 150 people, within roughly 200 m.
places.where: Region 1, lake shore at sea level, snowy temperate forest. On the map the village sits on the north rim of a broad bay of the long lake, forest behind, a pale clearing inland to the right. A Tùng Đào village. Nearest: Ngưng Yên Nhãn spirit vein 75 km.
places.imagined: A windless deep-winter dusk. Frozen smoke stands in pale columns over every chimney; children are being called in by the bell on its post at the ice edge, and a fish lies on the post's stone base.
places.subject: The place: Hàn Yên Thôn, the village of frozen smoke, on a snowy lake shore. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle, the village in the centre of the frame on a rim of snow-covered shore, the great silver lake below it with a broad strip of grey lake ice at its edge, and birch and spruce forest rising behind. The village: about twenty-five grey tile-roofed houses of timber and stone, each with an unusually tall stone chimney, clustered along two snowy lanes that run down to the shore and joined by a trampled square; between them wood stacks, small vegetable plots under snow, fish-drying racks, and a row of five boat sheds with upturned boats; a watch-house with a single slightly taller grey roof at the shore end. Smoke rises from every chimney in thin pale columns that stand perfectly straight, so tall they reach above the tree line and hang as frozen pillars, the dominant vertical lines of the picture. Signature element: at the very edge of the ice stands a single tall wooden post carrying a small bronze bell under a little grey roof, on a round stone base with a single fish laid on it, the bell glinting; a straight line of footprints leads to it from the village. Life at scale: a few tiny children running home, two fishers hauling a sled across the ice, a dog or two. Light and season: dead of winter at golden dusk, light from the upper left turning the smoke columns rose-gold, long blue shadows toward the lower right.

places.name: Noãn Ốc Thôn
places.size: A village of about 25 domed stone houses and one bath-house, perhaps 150 people with seasonal visitors, within about 200 m; the steaming bath-house is the largest structure.
places.where: Region 1, shore of the long lake at sea level, snowy temperate forest; on the map the same broad bay as Hàn Yên Thôn, on its north rim, 150 km apart. A Tùng Đào village. Nearest: Ôn Thủy Mạch spirit vein 158 km. A hot spring was found beneath the snow in 1015.
places.imagined: A bright still winter morning. The domed roofs look like loaves in the snow, the bath-house sends up a soft plume, and old cultivators in robes are queuing at the spring.
places.subject: The place: Noãn Ốc Thôn, the village of warm houses, on a snowy lake shore. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; the village in the middle of the frame on a gently sloping shore, the lake below with a strip of ice along the water's edge, birch and spruce forest behind. The village: about twenty-five round domed houses of thick fieldstone, half sunk into the ground so that only the domes and low doorways show, each capped by a little grey tile roof, clustered like loaves of bread around a central trampled square; the domes are nearly bare of snow because the walls hold warmth, so each stands as a dark circle in the white. A covered timber walkway links the nearer houses. Signature element: a plain long timber bath-house stands over a hot spring at the heart of the village, a steam plume rising from it and drifting out over the ice, with a second stone-walled open pool beside it where the snow has melted back into a perfect wet circle; a small two-storey guest lodge stands by it. Smoke from a few chimneys is flattened by the cold, and the trampled paths between the domes show as pale threads. Life at scale: a queue of tiny robed figures at the bath-house door, a woman carrying incense sticks, goats in a stone pen, a few villagers clearing the paths. Light and season: clear winter morning, golden light from the upper left, the steam backlit, long soft blue shadows toward the lower right.

places.name: Hạo Nguyệt Hồ
places.size: The biggest lake on the continent, a ribbon of water some 300 km long and 15-50 km wide; the picture shows a stretch of it and its shore at true scale, with a single causeway shrine as the only human work, a stone path about 2 km long.
places.where: Region 1, Lãnh Nguyệt Lâm, sea-level lake in temperate forest. On the map a long narrow blue band running north to south beside dark forest, a thin river joining it at the top left, a hill on the west shore. Nearest lakes: Hàn Kính Hồ 146 km, Tàng Châu Đàm 177 km, Tẩy Nguyệt Đàm 180 km. Hàm Nguyệt Trang holds its moon; the pearls feed the shore towns.
places.imagined: Low evening gold on pale silver water. A thin grey causeway leaves a tiny shrine on the near shore and runs straight out, ending in open water, with the far end of the lake lost in haze.
places.subject: The place: Hạo Nguyệt Hồ, the long silver lake of the northern forest. Setting: seen from very high above at a steep aerial angle; a vast narrow lake of pale silver water runs from the lower left corner diagonally up toward the horizon, tens of kilometres wide near the camera and dwindling into haze at the far end, between dark shores of conifer and birch that fill both sides of the frame to the edges. The near shore on the left has reed beds, pebbled coves, and thin rims of pale ice; faint pearl-farm stakes stand in neat lines in the shallows a long way apart, tiny dots. Signature element: on the near shore a tiny grey-roofed fishers' shrine stands on a stone platform, and from it a thin grey stone causeway, about two kilometres long and the width of a footpath, runs straight out over the water and stops abruptly in the open lake, its last stones glinting with wet; the causeway is the only straight line in the whole landscape. Beyond it the water is empty and unbroken to the horizon, and a low golden path of light lies across it. A few tiny fishing skiffs sit far apart, one tied at the causeway's end, specks of people at the shrine. A narrow trail runs from the shrine into the birch forest. The forest around the lake is vast and untouched, small clearings of lake villages visible as thin threads of smoke far along the shore. Light and season: late autumn evening, low warm gold from the upper left, cool blue-green shadows in the forest, a faint pale moon already rising over the far haze.

places.name: Phản Cảnh Lâm
places.size: The heart of the northern forest at true scale: a dome of old spruce and larch some 100 km across, filling the whole frame, with one sunken hollow about 3 km wide at its centre; no buildings at all, only a hunters' trail and a strip of bark on the last tree.
places.where: Region 1, Lãnh Nguyệt Lâm. Temperate forest at about 180 m elevation, on the map an unbroken carpet of dark forest with only a pale river edge at the upper right. Belongs to no sect; Tùng Đào patrols skirt its edge. Nearest: Sương Tùng Các 127 km, Phong Khẩu Thôn 180 km.
places.imagined: Dusk everywhere but one place. The whole forest has gone grey-blue and cold, and in its centre a hollow ringed by giant larches keeps an amber glow that does not fade.
places.subject: The place: Phản Cảnh Lâm, the Forest of the Returning Light, the deep heart of a northern forest. Setting: seen from very high above at a steep aerial angle; an unbroken sea of old dark spruce and larch fills the entire frame to every edge, rising gently toward the middle as a low dome, no clearings, no fields, no villages, a few pockets of snow on the high ground and a thin pale stream at one corner. The canopy lies in cool blue-green shadow. Signature element: at the exact centre is a sunken hollow about three kilometres across, ringed by a circle of giant old larches taller than all the trees around them, whose crowns glow amber-gold as if lit from within, with a soft pool of lingering evening light lying on the hollow's floor, a moss-gold clearing with a small dark pond; the glow is the only warm colour in the picture and every other colour is cold. A faint hunters' trail, barely visible as a thin line among the trees, runs in from the lower left and stops a little short of the ring. Along the trail, tiny strips of pale bark are tied at the trunks like pinpricks of white. No building, no smoke, no boats: only, at the very trail's end, one tiny figure with a staff turned toward the light. Light and season: just after sunset in early autumn, the forest in blue twilight, long soft shadows to the lower right from a last band of sun on the upper left canopy, the hollow's amber light contrasting hard against it.

places.name: Trầm Bích Đàm
places.size: A long still pool about 6 km by 1.5 km behind a reed bar, with the moon halls of a small sect built on piles over its middle: roughly 45 timber buildings and a few stilt walkways, about 60 people. A natural lake with a settled sect in it, so the lake is the picture and the halls are about 300 m across.
places.where: Region 1, Lãnh Nguyệt Lâm. Sea-level lake in temperate forest at the end of a long river-fed lake; on the map a narrow blue pool at the end of a stream, between rocky shoulders, on a line of lakes running north. The new seat of Hàm Nguyệt Trang since 412, 90 km from the Shore House. Water 42 %, Wood 28 %. The Pool of the Sunken Jade Disc.
places.imagined: A windless night with a full moon. The pool is so still the disc lies in it whole, and the stilt-halls glow with a few lanterns, their reflections unbroken.
places.subject: The place: Trầm Bích Đàm, the Pool of the Sunken Jade Disc, with the stilt-halls of a water-arts sect raised over it. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; a long dark still pool fills the middle of the frame, jade-green near the shores and almost black at the centre, hemmed by a reed bar at its lower end and by pine and spruce forest and grey rock shoulders on both sides; a thin stream runs out of it at the lower right. The halls: forty-five dark timber buildings with grey tile roofs raised on tall piles over the middle of the pool, in three clusters joined by long covered stilt walkways: an inner gate hall at the reed-bar end with a boat landing, a pair of long dormitory halls, a great moon hall with a wide open railed deck on its upper floor facing the water, and a slim lantern tower; small docks and floating pearl-washing rafts surround them, with a few skiffs. Signature element: the surface is utterly still, and the pool holds a perfect reflection of the halls and of a full pale moon, so every roof appears twice; one sunken disc of paler jade lies on the pool bed beneath the halls, a flat round shape some eighty metres across visible through the clear water, with a faint ring of reeds around it. Life at scale: tiny figures in pale robes sitting in a row on the moon hall's deck, a few lanterns lit along the walkways, a diver's raft at the edge. Light and season: late autumn dusk, the last golden light from the upper left on the western roofs and tree crowns, the pool darkening to blue and silver and the moon mirrored in it.

places.name: Cựu Châu Trấn
places.size: A ruined pearl town: once about 600 roofs and a harbour, now perhaps 150 broken walls and fallen roofs in a footprint of about 500 m by 300 m, with dead oyster beds in the shallows. Small, the size of a modest town after it was abandoned in 749.
places.where: Region 1, northern Lãnh Nguyệt Lâm. Sea-level temperate forest on a narrow arm of the lake beside a rocky headland; on the map a deep narrow inlet between two grey ridges, a thin river at its foot. Former town, held by Hàm Nguyệt Trang. Beds died when the lake froze to its bed in 748-749. Water 35 %, Wood 30 %. Nearest: Hồi Lưu Thôn village 79 km.
places.imagined: A grey, cold afternoon. Birches grow through the roofs of the old pearl hall, the quays are fallen into the shallows, and in the dead oyster beds a single line of fresh stakes shows someone is seeding them again.
places.subject: The place: Cựu Châu Trấn, the Old Pearl Town, a ruin on a narrow arm of the long lake. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; a deep narrow inlet of grey-green water fills the upper half, between two rocky grey ridges with dark conifer on top, and a thin stream enters from the lower left; the ruined town lies on the near shore on a gentle slope of long grass and young birch. The ruin: about a hundred and fifty broken buildings in the grid of a once-busy town, grey tile roofs collapsed into the walls, timber frames burned or rotted to blackened ribs, birches and saplings standing in the rooms; a long pearl hall with its ridge sagged in the middle, its courtyard full of fallen tiles; a main street running to a harbour, now half-buried in grass; broken stone quays slumping into the water, a collapsed harbour wall like a row of teeth, the stumps of old nest poles. In the shallows beyond, the rows of old oyster-bed stakes stand grey and bare in the clear water, lines of dark stumps; the water above them is pale and empty. Signature element: one short new line of pale fresh stakes among the old, and a single small skiff there, marking that someone is trying to seed the dead beds again. Life at scale: only a couple of tiny figures, a lone fisher in the skiff, a few crows. Light and season: a cold grey afternoon in late autumn, thin golden light breaking from the upper left onto the ruins, long soft shadows toward the lower right, ground mist along the water.

places.name: Thán Diêu Thôn
places.size: A charcoal-burners' village of about 15 houses with a row of 8 kilns and an ink hut, perhaps 80 people, set in a clearing about 250 m across, deliberately away from the trees.
places.where: Region 1, northern Lãnh Nguyệt Lâm, temperate forest at about 130 m on rolling hills; on the map a mix of grassy ridges and dark pine, small rocky pockets, a river at the upper right. A Hàm Nguyệt Trang village that burns pine soot for the ink of Sương Tùng Các. Wood 54 %. Nearest: Lạc Diệp Lâm forest 79 km.
places.imagined: A grey morning of low cloud. Smoke from eight kilns stands up black and blue, the clearing is bare and swept so no ember can reach the pines, and a man in the ink hut is grinding soot with a pestle.
places.subject: The place: Thán Diêu Thôn, the charcoal-kiln village of the high pines. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; rolling hills of old dark pine and a few grassy ridges fill the frame, with a thin stream at the upper right. In the middle a large bare swept clearing about two hundred and fifty metres across has been cut into the forest and ringed by a wide moat of bare dirt and a stone-edged firebreak so that no ember can reach the trees. The village: about fifteen low houses of timber and clay with grey tile roofs, round a small yard with a well, woodpiles stacked in neat cubes, and a long open-sided store of pine resin barrels; on the clearing's far side a row of eight round clay kilns shaped like beehives, each with a plume of smoke, some thin and white, others dark and heavy, the plumes bending in one direction with the wind; a low ink hut with a stone grinding floor and shelves of small black cakes drying in the open. Signature element: the kilns and the firebreak ring, a black circle of soot staining the earth around each kiln, and the bare clearing as pale as a plate against the dark pines. Life at scale: tiny figures with long rakes tending the kilns, a cart of resin on the track, a couple of children at the well. Light and season: a still late-summer morning under low cloud, golden light breaking from the upper left through the smoke, long soft shadows toward the lower right.

places.name: Sương Tùng Các
places.size: A minor sect of about 35 scribes, papermakers and lantern-carriers: a walled pine-wood compound of roughly 60 buildings in about 250 m, plus birch-bark paper yards and a ring of lantern frames. Founded only in 1060, so it is young, neat and smaller than an old house.
places.where: Region 1, high pines of Lãnh Nguyệt Lâm, temperate forest at about 250 m elevation; on the map a deep forest of dark pine and meadowy ridges, with a small bright yellow-gold glow of forest in the lower left, and a stream at the right edge. Vassal of Tùng Đào Cung, a house of talisman writers; Wood 58 %, Water 14 %. Nearest: Phản Cảnh Lâm 127 km, Sơn Ổ Thôn village 152 km.
places.imagined: Late autumn, the week of the lanterns. Hundreds of paper ward lanterns hang in rows from poles across the courtyards, being filled and counted before the carriers walk them round the lake.
places.subject: The place: Sương Tùng Các, the Pavilion of the Frosted Pines, a small sect of talisman writers who make birch-bark paper, pine-soot ink and ward lanterns. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; an old high pine forest of dark blue-green trees with frost-whitened crowns fills the frame, with meadowy ridges and a thin stream at the right. The compound: a pale timber palisade and low stone wall enclose about sixty buildings on a gentle south slope; a gate hall with a double roof on the lower side, a long writing hall with a tall pitched roof and a high row of narrow windows, a scripture library, a ward hall, dormitories, kitchens, and a small round hall near the back where a sealed box is kept; all of pine timber with steep shingled roofs dusted with frost. Beyond the wall, to one side: paper yards with long rows of birch bark laid out to dry in pale sheets, resin boiling vats with thin steam, racks of paper cut square, and a neat stack of pine-soot ink cakes under a lean-to. Signature element: hundreds of paper ward lanterns, pale round shapes on long poles in tidy rows across the courtyards and along the avenue outside the gate, ready for the autumn round of four hundred lanterns to the lake villages; a single path goes down the hill toward the lake. Life at scale: tiny figures in grey robes carrying lantern poles on their shoulders, a cart of lanterns, scribes bent over a drying line. Light and season: late autumn, thin golden light from the upper left, frost on the pine crowns, long soft shadows toward the lower right.

places.name: Hồng Lô Cốc
places.size: A minor alchemist sect of about 60 people (alchemists, furnace-men, cooks, boat crews, healers): around 70 buildings terraced up a coastal valley about 700 m long, with a landing, a satchel hall, and one great furnace tower about 40 m high. Founded 650, older and busier than the lake manors.
places.where: Region 1, north coast of the cape Tuyết Hỏa Giác. Tundra at about 300 m, on a snowy coastal slope on the volcano's flank; on the map a big oval bay of blue sea with two dark volcanic isles in it and snowy hills rimming the shore. Vassal of Thúy Vi Tông, alchemy (Fire, Water). Nearest: Kê Quan Khoáng mine 79 km, Hồ Tâm Thang hot spring 152 km.
places.imagined: A grey sea evening. The red furnace glows like a coal and the ring of bare black ground around it steams while snow falls everywhere else; a boat arrives from the isles carrying fire-stone.
places.subject: The place: Hồng Lô Cốc, the Valley of the Red Furnace, an alchemists' sect on a snowy volcanic coast. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; a steep coastal valley of snow-covered black rock opens at the bottom of the frame onto a grey-blue sea, with two dark volcanic isles smoking faintly in the bay beyond, and snowy hills rise to the upper edge. The sect: some seventy buildings climbing the valley in stepped stone terraces, grey stone halls under dark red tile roofs, connected by stairs and ramps: a small stone landing and boat shed at the water, a satchel hall for healers, long drying sheds for herbs, rows of dormitories, kitchens and storehouses of coal, then terraces rising to the top, where a squat, tall red-brick furnace tower stands, about forty metres high, with a glowing orange mouth at its base and a thin dark plume from its stack, the tallest outline on the cape. Signature element: around the tower a wide perfect ring of bare, dark, steaming ground, some two hundred metres across, where snow never settles, black and wet, its edge sharp against the white, with vapour rising and little glowing vents; fuel carts and lines of tiny figures cross it. Life at scale: a long boat with a dozen oarsmen unloading dark stone at the landing, furnace-men at the tower's mouth, apprentices catching snowflakes by the mouth, smoke from the kitchens. Light and season: deep winter late afternoon, golden light from the upper left on the snow and the red roofs, the furnace's orange glow strong in the shadow, long soft blue shadows toward the lower right.

places.name: Yên Ba Thành
places.size: A walled port city of some 25,000 roofs and perhaps 120,000 people, about 3 km by 2.5 km inside walls with several districts, a harbour mole 1.5 km long and a pagoda about 70 m tall. The busiest market of the cape, so it is dense, with a river-mouth harbour and ship yards.
places.where: Region 1, the cape Tuyết Hỏa Giác. A river mouth on the coast at sea level, temperate forest; on the map a green slope descending to the coast with a snowy rocky ridge running along the right, an open sea at the lower left. Thúy Vi Tông's port. Nearest: Lục Âm Lâm forest 75 km.
places.imagined: Dawn mist on the river. The lower streets and the quays are lost in blue-green haze while the green pagoda at the end of the mole stands clear above, its bronze horn sounding for the ships coming home.
places.subject: The place: Yên Ba Thành, the misty port city of the sect Thúy Vi, at a river mouth on a cold sea. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; the city fills the middle and left of the frame on a coastal slope, a snow-capped rocky ridge rising on the right with dark green forest on its flanks, the sea in the lower left with white wave lines, and a river entering from the upper middle. The city: a great rectangular walled port, its grey stone wall about three kilometres long with a dozen gate towers, enclosing some twenty-five thousand grey-tile roofs in districts: a dense river quarter of narrow streets and canals with stone bridges, a broad market quarter with a grid of warehouses and long shop rows, a shipwrights' district with slipways and hulls on stocks, a high terrace district of walled courtyards and a governor's hall with a big gate tower, and a drum tower at the main gate; a long stone harbour mole runs a kilometre and a half into the sea, with quays, cranes of timber, and many dozens of masted junks and barges at anchor and moored. Mist: a drifting blue-green haze veils the quays, lower streets and the river mouth, so that only roof ridges and masts poke through. Signature element: at the end of the long mole stands a tall slender pagoda of green-glazed tile about seventy metres high, rising clear above the mist with a small bronze horn at its peak, and a faint circular ring in the haze around the city marks the sect's fog-keeping array. Life at scale: tiny lines of porters and carts on the quays, hundreds of figures in the squares, a handful of junks under sail beyond the mole. Light and season: early morning, low golden light from the upper left, a late-autumn chill, long soft shadows toward the lower right.

places.name: Mục Ca Thành
places.size: A walled grassland city of about 12,000 low roofs and perhaps 60,000 people, walls about 2.2 km by 1.6 km, ringed by about 80 round dry-stone sheepfolds each some 30 m across. A wool-and-hide market, so wide and low with a harbour on the sea side, smaller than the port city of Yên Ba.
places.where: Region 1, the cape Tuyết Hỏa Giác. Open coastal grassland, sea level; on the map a long green island, a chain of two bent islands in a wide blue sea. Thúy Vi Tông city. Nearest: Bàn Căn Huyệt spirit vein 79 km, Khuynh Mộc Lâm forest 125 km, Phong Phàm Thôn 158 km. Founded 700.
places.imagined: Dusk on the grass. Herders sing from fold to fold across the ring around the walls, each family with its own tune, while the flocks are counted in.
places.subject: The place: Mục Ca Thành, the Herders' Song city, a wool-and-hide market on open coastal grassland. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; rolling green-gold grassland covers the upper and middle frame, a shingle shore and a short stretch of the grey-blue sea at the lower edge, a small harbour on the sea side. The city: a rectangular wall of grey stone about two kilometres long, low and plain, with a modest gate tower the tallest roof in the place, enclosing some twelve thousand low grey-tile roofs in long wind-hunched rows along streets that run straight from the main gate to the harbour gate; a large wool exchange with a long yard, rows of hide-tanning sheds along a stream, a central square, grain warehouses, and a small stone harbour with a short pier and a dozen boats. Signature element: strung around the outside of the walls in a wide ring, about eighty round dry-stone sheepfolds, each a pale stone circle some thirty metres across on the green grass, spaced like beads on a string and each holding a flock of tiny white specks, with paths linking them to the gates; the ring is clear even from the height. Beyond the ring more flocks drift over the grass in loose cloud-like pockets, and herd dogs show as tiny dark commas. Life at scale: carts on the roads, riders driving flocks, small figures at the folds, smoke from the tanneries. Light and season: late summer dusk, golden light from the upper left raking over the grass and the stone circles, long soft shadows to the lower right.

places.name: Bạch Sa Trấn
places.size: A small walled fishing-and-trading town of about 1,200 roofs, a wall about 500 m by 350 m, perhaps 5,000 people, with 40 long net frames on the beach. A town (a thousand or more roofs), and the biggest place on its little island.
places.where: Region 1, an island off the cape Tuyết Hỏa Giác: grassland and white sand beaches at sea level; on the map a bent grey-green island with a rocky nub in a turquoise-edged sea, small separate islets to the south-west. Thúy Vi Tông town. Nearest: Sam Ảnh Lâm forest 79 km. Founded 380 by the Thẩm family.
places.imagined: Late afternoon. White net frames stretch along the beach so the town seems fenced in white lattice, boats are drawn up on the white sand, and the shallows are pale turquoise.
places.subject: The place: Bạch Sa Trấn, the White Sand town, a fishing town on an island beach. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; a broad beach of bright white sand fills the middle of the frame, grassland and a rocky green headland behind, pale turquoise shallows deepening to dark blue at the lower edge. The town: a small rectangular walled town of whitewashed walls and grey-tile roofs, about five hundred metres long, some twelve hundred roofs on a grid of lanes with a taller whitewashed clan hall at its centre, a market square, salting sheds, a fish market, and a stone gate to the beach; a short wooden pier runs into the shallows with a dozen fishing boats drawn up on the sand and moored. Signature element: in long parallel rows along the beach in front of the walls stand about forty whitewashed net-drying frames, each some thirty metres long, forming a white lattice that seems to fence the town from the sea, with nets hung on them in pale sheets; behind them the white sand makes the whole shore dazzling. Beyond the walls a cart track runs along the dunes to a small stone landing, and wet sand shows dark where the tide has just left it. Life at scale: women mending nets, tiny figures pushing boats, children on the sand, a cart on the shore track, a few gulls. Light and season: late afternoon in early autumn, strong golden light from the upper left on the white walls and frames, long soft shadows to the lower right, the shallows luminous turquoise.

places.name: Mạch Lãng Thôn
places.size: A farming village of about 12 grey-roofed farmhouses with wheat strips covering about a square kilometre, perhaps 70 people; the fields are the main thing, not the houses.
places.where: Region 1, the cape Tuyết Hỏa Giác: a green volcanic island at sea level, grassland, on a gentle coastal slope; on the map a pair of bent islands in a wide sea. Thúy Vi Tông village. Nearest: Hải Tùng Lâm forest 141 km, Khuynh Mộc Lâm 160 km, Mục Ca Thành 226 km.
places.imagined: Harvest time. The gold strips of wheat ripple like waves down to the sea, and the last strip is left standing for the wind to thresh.
places.subject: The place: Mạch Lãng Thôn, the Wheat Wave village, a farming village on warm volcanic soil by the sea. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; a gentle coastal slope of black volcanic soil covers the frame, with the grey-blue sea along the lower edge and a narrow dark beach. The village: about twelve grey-tile farmhouses with barns and threshing floors, set in a loose line along a lane partway up the slope, each with a yard wall of black lava stone, a well and a woodpile. Signature element: a square kilometre of long, narrow, golden wheat strips running in parallel lines down the slope to the shore, divided by low walls of black lava stone so the gold and black alternate like stripes, the wheat rippling in the wind in visible waves; one strip left standing at the end of the harvest while the neighbouring ones are cut into pale stubble and sheaves. A narrow dark beach at the bottom with one small boat, and a cart track winding down to it. Life at scale: tiny harvesters in a line with sickles, sheaf stacks, a cart drawn by a pair of oxen, children on top of a sheaf pile. Light and season: harvest afternoon, warm golden light raking from the upper left across the wheat and throwing the lava walls into long soft shadows to the lower right. Along the lava walls run low hedges of salt-grass, and each strip has a small stone cairn at its upper end marking the family that tills it. A winding cart track divides the village from the shore, and a few haystacks stand like pale domes by the threshing floor. The sea beyond the narrow beach is a clear green-blue with white lines of foam, and the black volcanic sand makes a dark stripe between the gold fields and the water.

places.name: Phong Phàm Thôn
places.size: A pilots' village of about 35 grey-roofed houses, boat sheds and a slipway, perhaps 180 people, on a headland about 400 m across; the wind mast on the tip is about 25 m tall.
places.where: Region 1, the cape Tuyết Hỏa Giác: a green headland on a chain of bent islands in a wide sea, grassland at sea level. Thúy Vi Tông village. Nearest: Khuynh Mộc Lâm forest 90 km, Mục Ca Thành 158 km.
places.imagined: A strong clear morning. Every family's streamer streams out from the mast at the headland's tip in a different colour, and sailors read them before launching.
places.subject: The place: Phong Phàm Thôn, the Wind Sail village of coast pilots, on a windy grassy headland. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; a green headland of windblown grass and grey rocks runs out into a deep blue sea, with white wave lines around it. The village: about thirty-five grey-tile houses on the headland's neck, in short rows along a lane with stone-walled yards, drying racks for sails and rope, a rope-walk, a pilots' hall, and below on the sheltered shore boat sheds and a stone slipway with a dozen small sailboats drawn up. Signature element: on the very tip of the headland stands a tall wooden wind mast about twenty-five metres high, trailing hundreds of long cloth streamers in many colours, red, yellow, blue, green, white, each family's own, all flying in the same direction and making a bright ribbon of colour against the grass and sea; a small stone platform at its foot. Life at scale: tiny sailors at the mast reading the streamers, children running with small streamers, a small sailboat leaving the slip under a full sail. Light and season: a clear windy morning, bright golden light from the upper left catching the streamers, long soft shadows to the lower right, whitecaps on the sea. Between the houses run narrow lanes of beaten earth edged with upturned boats used as sheds, and rope coils hang on every porch post. The grass on the headland is cropped short and flattened by the wind into long combed streaks, all leaning one way, and white gulls ride the updraft above the mast. The sea below the slipway shows a clear pale shallow band, then a darker deep channel where small sails cross.

places.name: Hòa Thử Thôn
places.size: A farming village of about 20 grey-roofed houses with about 60 granary huts on stone stilts, perhaps 110 people, on millet fields about a square kilometre.
places.where: Region 1, an island of the cape Tuyết Hỏa Giác, grassland at sea level with a rocky nub; on the map a bent island with an orange-brown inland patch. Thúy Vi Tông village. Nearest: Thúy Bình Phong peak 79 km, Sam Ảnh Lâm 180 km. Fed Yên Ba through the winter of 860.
places.imagined: Harvest feast. Rows of small granary huts on their mushroom stilts stand in the stubble, one hut in every row left empty, and the millet wine is being poured.
places.subject: The place: Hòa Thử Thôn, the Granary village, a farming village among millet fields near the shore. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; a gentle plain of yellow millet and green field strips runs to the coast, with a small boat landing on a pebble shore at the lower right and a rocky green rise behind. The village: about twenty grey-tile farmhouses with yards in a loose cluster, cart tracks between them, a threshing floor and a well. Signature element: neat rows of about sixty small square granary huts with grey tile roofs, each raised on mushroom-shaped stone stilts about a metre high, stood in regular lines on the field edge, each row with one hut left empty and its door shut and painted pale; the huts throw short square shadows under the raised floors. Field strips in yellow, green and brown tilework around the village, a cart track to the landing. Life at scale: tiny harvesters bringing in millet, a cart loaded with sacks, a feast table set under a tree with small figures around it. Light and season: autumn harvest afternoon, warm golden light from the upper left, short crisp shadows under the granaries, long soft ones to the lower right. Between the field strips run narrow cart tracks edged with drystone, and near the landing a threshing floor of beaten earth shows as a pale disc where the sheaves are being flailed. A short line of drying racks holds millet heads in the sun, and a low stone well stands under a single big tree at the village centre. The shore beyond is pale pebble, with the water a clear green-blue close in and darker further out.

places.name: Ẩn Loan Thôn
places.size: A hidden cliff-top village of about 8 grey-roofed houses with a zigzag stair, a small cove and a sea cave, perhaps 50 people, in about 120 m.
places.where: Region 1, an island off the cape Tuyết Hỏa Giác: grassland on a cliff at sea level; on the map a bent island with a rocky nub, a small islet to the south-west. Thúy Vi Tông village. Nearest: Vân Tước Thôn 79 km, Hoàng Thổ Nhãn 112 km. A pirate crew once hid in the cove.
places.imagined: A grey-green evening. From the cliff top the stair zigzags down to the dark sea cave, one rowing boat waits on the pebbles, and the village shows nothing to the open sea.
places.subject: The place: Ẩn Loan Thôn, the Hidden Cove village, a handful of houses above a narrow cove between cliffs. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; a green cliff-top meadow on the upper half of the frame, with the sea below it, deep green in a narrow cove and dark blue beyond, the cove walled by pale rock cliffs on both sides so that the open sea cannot see in. The village: about eight grey-tile houses with stone walls in a short row along the cliff edge, each with a small yard, a vegetable plot and a woodpile, with a goat pen and a tiny shrine. Signature element: a steep stair cut into the cliff face, zigzagging down in some fifteen switchbacks to a dark sea cave mouth at the waterline, with a small pebble beach before it and a single rowing boat pulled up; the cove is partly in shadow and the stair's steps catch the light. A path leads from the village to the headland above. Life at scale: a couple of tiny figures on the stair carrying baskets, a woman watching from the cliff, a gull or two. Light and season: grey-green evening in late summer, golden light from the upper left on the cliff-top grass, the cove in cool shadow, long soft shadows to the lower right. The grass on the cliff top is cropped by goats and edged by wind-bent thorn, and a low drystone wall keeps the cliff path from the vegetable plots. At the cove's far side a second faint ledge path runs to a ruined drystone hut once used by the pirates. Below, the water in the cove is dark green over rock, with slow white foam lines at its mouth, and seaweed beds show as dark strips along the cliff foot.
